source.table: Table 5. Outlays of the U.S. Government, May 2026 and Other Periods
source.title: Department of Energy section (Table-5 cap-fit unit, pages 12-13; the section spans the page break -- NNSA + Environmental and Other Defense Activities on p12, Energy Programs onward on p13). Full 9-column outlays model. Reclassified from over-cap to cap-fit by the 2026-07-15 sizing pass (132 cells). NESTED (family 3): Energy Programs rolls its eight lines into Total--Energy Programs; NNSA and Environmental and Other Defense Activities have no printed subtotals, so their lines feed the department total directly. Energy Programs' Applicable column is single-source (only its 'Other' line), handled like -homeland-security / -state. Family pattern: plans/treasury-mts-2026-05-outlays-table5.md; worked examples: -homeland-security, -state.
source.period: May FY2026 (This Month = May 2026; Current FYTD = Oct 2025 - May 2026; Prior FYTD = Oct 2024 - May 2025)

unit_note: USD millions ('[$ millions]' per table header). Table 5 legend (p. 23): '......' = 'No Transactions' (omitted); '(**)' = 'Less than absolute value of $500,000' (omitted). The 'Defense Nuclear Waste Disposal' row (under Environmental and Other Defense Activities) is dropped entirely -- every one of its cells is '(**)'. Values as printed, thousands separators stripped, negatives as leading '-'. Nine-column model: 3 periods x (Gross Outlays / Applicable Receipts / Outlays[net]). Energy Programs nests (family 3); its Applicable column has a single contributing line ('Other'), so the Energy Programs gross/net columns roll up but the Applicable column does not -- the Total--Energy Programs applicable cells (c2/c5/c8) are marked leaf and covered by the Energy Programs total-row net identity, while the 'Other' line-level applicable is covered by its own net identity. At the department level the Applicable column has three sources (Total--Energy Programs, Power Marketing Administration, Proprietary), so it rolls up normally. Non-default tolerances quote the Table-5 rounding note (p. 23): 'Note: Details may not add to totals due to rounding.' Energy Programs sums eight independently-rounded lines, so several roll-ups and identities carry a +/-1 gap; all values are render-verified.
